description: An automatic dry-pet-food dispenser with a rotating body containing several equal-sized compartments, each closed by a spring-loaded trap door at the bottom. A drive mechanism periodically withdraws a support bar holding a trap door shut, letting that compartment's food fall by gravity through a directional trough into the pet's bowl below, dispensing one measured portion at a time on a schedule. UNIQUE ADDITION (not in the source patent): the dispenser also has a small load cell built into the bowl itself that weighs how much food the pet actually ate versus how much was dispensed, and if a portion goes mostly uneaten for several consecutive feedings, it automatically reduces future portion sizes and sends a low-appetite alert to the owner's phone.
concepts: rotating body defines multiple equal-sized food compartments
each compartment is closed at the bottom by a spring-loaded trap door
a drive mechanism periodically withdraws a support bar that holds a trap door shut
released food falls by gravity through a directional trough into the bowl below
the dispenser meters one measured portion at a time on a schedule
a load cell built into the bowl measures food actually eaten versus food dispensed
if a portion remains mostly uneaten for several consecutive feedings, future portion sizes are reduced
when low appetite is detected, an alert is sent to the owner's phone

patents.title: Automatic dry pet food dispenser
patents.rationale: This excerpt shares measured dry-food dispensing from like-sized compartments using bottom trap-door panels, a withdrawing draw bar, and a directional trough that drops food into a bowl on a timed basis. It does not disclose bowl load-cell measurement of eaten versus dispensed food, adaptive reduction of future portions after repeated leftovers, or any low-appetite phone alert.

recommendations: Tie the bowl load cell to a per-feeding tare-and-settle routine that records only post-dispense consumption, so the system can distinguish actual eating from transient bowl movement or kibble bounce.

Add a multi-feeding intake trend rule that reduces portion size only after a defined number of consecutive low-consumption events, with an additional check against body-weight or activity baseline to avoid false appetite alarms.

Log each compartment release with a compartment-index identifier and a delivered-mass estimate, then reconcile that log against the bowl weight trace to confirm that the scheduled portion was actually dispensed and consumed.

Include a trap-door position sensor or support-bar travel sensor that confirms a full release event before the controller marks the portion as delivered, and trigger a retry or jam alert if the release signature is incomplete.
Use a density-calibration table or learnable kibble-mass profile so that the scheduled portion is converted from volume to true mass for each food type before adaptive portion reduction is applied.
Send the low-appetite alert only after packaging the last several feeding events into a concise trend report that includes dispensed mass, consumed mass, and the portion-reduction history.
Add a caregiver override that freezes automatic portion reduction until the owner or veterinarian approves a new appetite baseline after illness, medication, or food change.

Correlate the bowl weight signal with a brief post-dispense stabilization window and a leftover-threshold check before issuing the alert, so uneaten food sitting in the bowl is distinguished from food that was merely eaten slowly.
